close_reason: Added impl std::fmt::Display + impl std::error::Error for SlowModeError. Three regression tests lock in the contract using UTCDate::from with hardcoded RFC 3339 strings as independent oracles (not values derived from the impl under test): Display content check, compile-time Error trait bound check, Box<dyn Error> coercion check. No analog in mail-server (slow_mode_check is chat-spec only per JMAP-x2gd.67 cross-walk), so this is chat-server-LOCAL. Commit 7b82d34. clippy --all-targets + rustdoc -D warnings + 21 lib tests all green.
description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:222-226

  #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  pub struct SlowModeError {
      pub retry_after: jmap_types::UTCDate,
  }

The type is literally named *Error and is used as the error arm
of Result<(), SlowModeError> in the slow_mode_check trait method
(backend.rs:717-724):

  fn slow_mode_check(...) -> impl std::future::Future<
      Output = Result<(), SlowModeError>
  > + Send {...}

But:

1. No `impl std::error::Error for SlowModeError`. Any downstream
   code that wants to convert via the std error trait — e.g.
   `let _: Box<dyn std::error::Error> = my_err.into()` — has to
   write a manual `From` impl.

2. No `impl std::fmt::Display for SlowModeError`. `eprintln!('{}',
   err)` does not compile. `format!('{err}')` does not compile.
   `anyhow::Error::from(slow_mode_error)` does not compile because
   anyhow requires `std::error::Error` (which transitively
   requires Display).

Contract effect on consumers:

- A consumer writing custom diagnostics ('slow-mode rate limit
  hit by user X on chat Y, retry after Z') cannot use the
  standard Rust error machinery on SlowModeError. They must
  hand-write `format!('rate limited, retry after {}',
  err.retry_after.as_ref())` everywhere.

- A consumer integrating with tracing's `?` field-formatter
  (`tracing::warn!(error = ?err, ...)`) gets the Debug repr
  (acceptable), but `tracing::warn!(error = %err, ...)` does
  not compile.

- A consumer that wants to bubble the error up through `?` into
  their own `MyAppError` enum has to add an explicit `From<SlowModeError>` —
  fine, but the typical Rust pattern is `#[from]` via thiserror, which
  requires the wrapped type implement `std::error::Error`.

Engineering basis: Rust's standard error-handling story explicitly
requires Error + Display. Naming a struct `*Error` and not
implementing the traits is a workspace-wide reader trap. Compare
to MemoryError (memory.rs:432) which:

  impl std::fmt::Display for MemoryError { ... }
  impl std::error::Error for MemoryError {}

(noted by the explore subagent — these impls exist for
MemoryError but not SlowModeError).

Recommended fix:

  impl std::fmt::Display for SlowModeError {
      fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
          write!(f, 'slow-mode rate limit; retry after {}',
              self.retry_after.as_ref())
      }
  }
  impl std::error::Error for SlowModeError {}

Or derive via thiserror if the workspace already pulls it (it
does not currently — but adding it for this is overkill; the
two impls above are 8 lines).

This is correctness for the contract: a *Error type that doesn't
satisfy Error is broken contract from the caller's perspective.
title: API contract: SlowModeError lacks std::error::Error and std::fmt::Display impls
